verdict: PASS as audited transcription and pinned raw-step parity
review_mode: Independent source/archived-body and exact-source log review; no builds, downloads or edits

source_archive.note: Manifest references separate full body files rather than embedding them; all four referenced body hashes were checked. Preserve those bodies together when making durable.

findings: All10 binary opcodes in the local runtime word subset and unary ISZERO are represented. Source arithmetic first-pop x/second-pop y is preserved: ADD lines40-49, SUB67-76 and MUL94-103 use wrapping operations; DIV121-133 pops dividend then divisor and explicitly returns0 on zero divisor. Natural SUB(size-y+x)%size is valid for the typed UInt256 inputs, including underflow; no assertion for arbitrary unbounded natural inputs is made.

Comparison source pops left then right for LT36-45, GT89-98 and EQ142-151; ISZERO169-177 uses the sole popped word. Lean predicates and their 0/1 encodings match these directions, not a reversed convention masked by commutativity.

Bitwise AND36-43 matches natural AND; the proof derives its result below UInt256.size. SHL171-183 and SHR201-213 pop shift first and value second. Lean pinned mapping explicitly reverses function arguments to shiftLeft/Right(value,shift); mask/mod equivalence and zero for shift>=256 are proved. SHR modulo elimination follows its result<=input bound.

value_parity is a universally quantified theorem for typed words, covering zero divisor, modular overflow/underflow and shifts256 or greater without finite examples or native_decide. It compares independently written natural transcription to pinned word functions.

step_parity and isZero_step use actual pureStep_sound for the listed opcodes with exact input stack decomposition and prove actual raw EvmYul.step successful result, preserving state except stack/PC through replaceStackAndIncrPC. The binary reference word is not merely asserted equal to the existing implementation.

Python stack.pop() removes the list end and stack.append adds there; fromPython reverses it. python_binary proves base++[y,x] maps to x::y::reverse(base), with result append mapping to result-head-cons. This is an encoding identity, not a Python execution theorem.
assumptions_and_limits: Audited source-to-transcription and ethereum_types.numeric wrapping/shift/comparison implementation are explicit boundaries; the module does not execute Python or prove numeric-library refinement.

Raw-step parity assumes sufficient stack shape, but does not prove actual reference gas/stack error-control flow, EVM Z acceptance, gas adequacy, PC representation correspondence or reference program execution.
Memory, storage, environment, jumps, PUSH/DUP/SWAP and wrapper settlement need their own adapters; this covers the local arithmetic/comparison/bitwise subset only.
The source manifest alone is not a full-body archive; durable integration must retain its four referenced files or embed their text. No new normative pin adoption is asserted.
